title: Keigo Higashino, Japanese Mystery Master Beloved Across Asia, Dies at 68
excerpt: The author of The Devotion of Suspect X — adapted into the Netflix India hit Jaane Jaan — died of colorectal cancer on July 23, leaving behind a body of work that reshaped crime fiction across continents.
body:
• Keigo Higashino, Japan's bestselling mystery novelist and the most popular novelist in China, died of colorectal cancer on July 23 at age 68
  • His novel The Devotion of Suspect X was adapted into the 2023 Netflix India film Jaane Jaan, starring Kareena Kapoor Khan, which became the most-viewed Indian film on the platform globally
  • Higashino won every major Japanese literary award including the Naoki Prize, and nearly 20 of his works were adapted into films and TV series
  • He served as president of the Mystery Writers of Japan from 2009 to 2013 and published over 80 novels across a four-decade career

Keigo Higashino, the Japanese mystery novelist whose intricately plotted crime fiction earned him a readership stretching from Tokyo to Mumbai, died on July 23 from colorectal cancer. He was 68.

His funeral was held privately by his family, according to Japanese media reports. No public memorial has been announced.

A Career Built on Subversion

Higashino spent four decades redefining what a mystery novel could do. Born in 1958 in the Ikuno-ku ward of Osaka to a working-class family, he studied electrical engineering at Osaka Prefecture University before winning the Edogawa Rampo Prize in 1985 for his debut novel After School. He quit his engineering job at Nippon Denso (now DENSO) a year later to write full time.

https://x.com/AFP/status/2081706178698969467

His breakthrough came in 2005 with The Devotion of Suspect X, which won the Naoki Prize — Japan's most prestigious literary award — after five previous nominations. The novel inverted the classic whodunit structure: readers learn the killer's identity early, and the tension comes from watching a brilliant mathematician construct an elaborate cover-up. The book won the Honkaku Mystery Award and was ranked the top mystery novel of the year by multiple Japanese guide books.

"I want Western readers to read my work and come to understand how Japanese people think, love and hate. I want them to be impressed that there is a Japanese person who came up with such unusual stories."

— Keigo Higashino

The India Connection

Higashino's influence reached India directly through the 2023 Netflix film Jaane Jaan (released internationally as Suspect X), an adaptation of The Devotion of Suspect X directed by Sujoy Ghosh and starring Kareena Kapoor Khan, Jaideep Ahlawat, and Vijay Varma. The film broke Netflix's record for the biggest opening weekend viewership for an Indian title and became the most-viewed Indian film on the platform globally by viewing hours.

The adaptation had been in development for nearly a decade. Director Ghosh first acquired the rights in 2014, cycling through multiple casting configurations — including Saif Ali Khan and Kangana Ranaut — before landing on the final ensemble. The film earned eight nominations at the Filmfare OTT Awards, winning three including Best Web Original Film (Critics).

Asia's Mystery King

Higashino was reportedly the most popular novelist in China, where his translated works dominated bestseller lists for years. His books were translated into at least six languages, and translation rights sold across China, Thailand, France, Russia, and Spain. Nearly 20 of his novels were adapted into films and TV series across Japan, South Korea, and China.

By 2018, he had published 66 novels and 20 short story collections. His Detective Galileo series — featuring the physics professor Manabu Yukawa — and the Police Detective Kaga series became pillars of modern Japanese crime fiction. Both series were translated into English by Minotaur Books.

Beyond mysteries, Higashino wrote children's stories and essays. His work frequently incorporated scientific elements — nuclear power, brain transplantation — alongside sports references drawn from his own experience as a university archery club captain.

Legacy

Higashino received the Medal with Purple Ribbon from the Japanese government in 2023 and the Kikuchi Kan Prize the same year. After the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake, he donated royalties from 100,000 reprinted copies of The Wings of the Kirin to relief efforts.

He was known for avoiding publicity, preferring that people not recognize him on the street. His final published works in English — Guilt and The Keeper of the Camphor Tree — were released by Minotaur Books in 2026.

He is survived by his family. A career spanning over 80 novels, multiple literary prizes, and adaptations across five countries leaves behind one of the most consequential bodies of work in modern Asian crime fiction.
